mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when UNRATE > 5.0% is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their respective 3-month moving averages signals robust economic activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when both HOUST and INDPRO are above their 3-month moving averages is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined as FEDFUNDS rising for 3 consecutive months above 1.0%), the increased cost of borrowing and reduced liquidity lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising for 3 consecutive months and FEDFUNDS > 1.0%
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return during monetary tightening cycles (as defined) is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A retail and food services sales level above $450 billion (RSAFS > 450,000) indicates robust consumer spending, which drives corporate revenue growth and results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return when RSAFS > 450,000 is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 95.0 (INDPRO < 95.0) indicates a weakening industrial sector, which reduces corporate output and profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when INDPRO < 95.0 is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day forward return when PAYEMS is rising and UNRATE is falling is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index above 2.5% (CPIAUCSL annual inflation > 2.5%) signals persistent inflation, which prompts central bank tightening and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when CPIAUCSL annual inflation > 2.5% is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
